- When sentiment shows strong positive spikes (≥0.67) followed by rapid decline, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment change is consistently negative (e.g., -0.33 to -1.00) over recent days, model often undercorrects — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.
- Model frequently overestimates prices after news volume spikes (≥3.0) — reduce forecast by 3–8% if news volume >2.0 in prior 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, model often lags — forecast should be 1–2% ahead of true price for 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a spike, model often fails to adjust — apply “lag correction” by subtracting 1–3% from forecast 2–3 days after peak.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is rising — increase forecast by 2–5% if sentiment <0.33 and price >previous 3-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility — smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ price + sentiment-weighted adjustment (e.g., +0.5x sentiment change).
